title: Topology of algebraic stacks and openness of flat locally presented maps
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. An algebraic stack over $S$ means a stack in groupoids with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; stacks, representability and 2-fibre products have the conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], smoothness is [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and algebraic spaces are [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For an algebraic stack $\mathcal X/S$, let $|\mathcal X|$ be the set of field-valued objects $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathcal X$, where $K$ is a field [def-weil-field, def-weil-affine-spectrum], modulo the equivalence identifying objects that become 2-isomorphic over a common field extension. Composition defines $|f|$ for a morphism of algebraic stacks. There is a topology on these point sets, agreeing with the usual topology on algebraic spaces [def-a1-space-point-topology], characterized by the following rule: for any smooth surjective scheme atlas $p:U\to\mathcal X$, a subset $W\subseteq|\mathcal X|$ is open if and only if $|p|^{-1}(W)$ is open in $|U|$; this rule is independent of the atlas. Every morphism of algebraic stacks induces a continuous map on point spaces. For every algebraic space $A/S$ and every flat locally finitely presented morphism $q:A\to\mathcal X$, the map $|q|:|A|\to|\mathcal X|$ is open. Here flatness and local finite presentation are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology] to the algebraic stacks in the statement. It supplies the atlas-independent topology, agreement with the usual scheme and algebraic-space topologies, and continuity of every morphism. Its closed-subset atlas criterion gives the required open-subset criterion by taking complements: $|p|^{-1}(|\mathcal X|\setminus W)=|U|\setminus|p|^{-1}(W)$. Composition on point classes is well-defined because a functor preserves the isomorphism over a common extension witnessing equivalence. It remains to prove openness for $q$.

proof.text: Fix a smooth surjective scheme atlas $p:U\to\mathcal X$. By [lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-space-source-representability], $q$ is representable by algebraic spaces, so $P=A\times_{\mathcal X}U$ is an algebraic space. Write $r:P\to A$ and $s:P\to U$. The chartwise base-change assertion of [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] gives that $s$, the base change of $q$, is flat and locally of finite presentation. By [lem-sfb-flat-lfp-space-universally-open], $|s|$ is open. The algebraic spaces $P$ and $A$ are algebraic stacks whose point topologies are the usual ones, so the continuity clause of [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology] makes $|r|$ continuous; thus for any open $O\subseteq|A|$, $|r|^{-1}(O)$ is open in $|P|$.

source.place: Tag 04XL (lemma-topology-points), final paragraph; Tag 04XC (lemma-property-spaces-too) for base change; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 042S (lemma-fppf-open)

proof.text: For open $O\subseteq|A|$, we have $|p|^{-1}(|q|(O))=|s|(|r|^{-1}(O))$. One inclusion follows from the tautological 2-isomorphism $qr\simeq ps$. For the reverse inclusion, take $u$ on the left and $a\in O$ with $|p|(u)=|q|(a)$. Choose field-valued representatives of $u,a$. Their equal image classes mean that, over a common field extension $M$, their images in $\mathcal X$ are isomorphic. The two pulled-back objects and that isomorphism are an object of the 2-fibre product $P$ over $M$, whose point maps to $u,a$. Hence $u$ lies on the right. The right side is open by step 2. The atlas criterion of [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology], in its complement form from step 1, implies that $|q|(O)$ is open. This proves openness for all $O$, without any surjectivity assumption on $q$.

lean.statement: theorem stackPointTopology_flat_lfp_open {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : BasedCategory.{v₁, w₁} (Over S)) (hF : IsAlgebraicModuliStack F) : (∀ (U : Over S) (p : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj U)) F), IsSmoothModuliAtlas F U p → ∀ W : Set (ModuliPoints F), IsOpen W ↔ IsOpen (moduliSchemePointMap p ⁻¹' W)) ∧ (∀ (G : BasedCategory.{v₂, w₂} (Over S)), IsAlgebraicModuliStack G → ∀ f : BasedFunctor F G, Continuous (moduliPointMap f)) ∧ (∀ (A : AlgebraicSpace S) (q : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli A.obj.obj) F), ModuliSpaceTest @Flat q → ModuliSpaceTest @LocallyOfFinitePresentation q → IsOpenMap (moduliPointMap q ∘ moduliSpacePointMap A.obj.obj))
lean.note: Uses the landed algebraic-moduli-stack and DM-morphism-properties nodes for the general stack predicate, field-object quotient, induced point map and chartwise scheme tests. The module constructs the topology and residue-field/Yoneda comparison maps with real data; separate statements give algebraic-space topology agreement and the atlas/continuity/openness clauses. No existing point quotient is redefined.

reviewed_lean.note: The statement is unchanged from live; the delivery adds the Lean record and two landed definition nodes to stmt_deps (def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack, def-sfb-dm-stack-morphism-properties), whose records cover every declaration used, and lean.statement matches the file verbatim. Checked against Stacks 04XG/04XL: (1) for every smooth surjective scheme atlas p, IsOpen W iff the preimage under moduliSchemePointMap p (the residue-field Yoneda point map) is open; the topology is the iSup of coinduced topologies over all smooth atlases, so a set is open iff open on every atlas, with no atlas chosen and real data, matching the existing AlgebraicSpace.pointTopologicalSpace pattern; (2) every morphism to an algebraic stack G (independent universes) is continuous, with no representability hypothesis; (3) every q from an algebraic space that passes ModuliSpaceTest for Flat and for LocallyOfFinitePresentation (the existing chartwise tests) gives an open map, with the usual topology on algebraic-space points and no surjectivity hypothesis. Agreement with algebraic spaces is a separate declared homeomorphism theorem for the canonical Yoneda comparison; its well-definedness sorry theorem is true. No extra hypotheses (DM, finiteness) or universe restrictions. The field-point quotient and moduliPointMap are reused, not redefined. Mathlib's Quot topology cannot compete with the new instance, since ModuliFieldObject is a plain def. No other stack-point topology exists; the sibling lem-sfb-stack-point-topology has lean null. Edge cases checked: empty stack, empty U, empty A, empty O, non-algebraic F, non-surjective q, nontrivial stabilizers, identity scheme atlas, universes. Docstrings carry source places, blueprint ids and the three proof steps; all theorems are sorry; no pro-etale substitute; no file changed or compiled.
